facts.value: Nurses in Canada practice in a wide variety of settings, with various levels of training and experience. They provide evidence-based care and educate their patients about health and disease.
Seven National Historic Sites of Canada related to nursing have been designated.

Five nurses' residences were designated in commemoration of the growing professionalism of nursing: the Ann Baillie Building, Begbie Hall, Hersey Pavilion, Pavillon Mailloux, and the St. Boniface Hospital Nurses' Residence.
La Corne Nursing Station and the Wilberforce Red Cross Outpost were designated in part to honor the role played by nurses in delivering health care to isolated areas.
Every nurse registered in the General or Extended class is required under the Registered Health Professions Act, 1991, to participate in the Quality Assurance (QA) program.
Nurses demonstrate their commitment to continually improving their practice by annually engaging in a written reflection, an analysis of the year, and setting two learning goals.
